detail: In the lead-up to an election in which economic concerns dominate, there was no clear front-runner. Minor parties will most likely determine who governs. (The New York Times)

wellington.title: What to Watch as New Zealand Votes Saturday
detail: Polls open at 3 p.m. ET Friday and close at 1 a.m. ET Saturday, with National and Labour level in the polls and Opportunity possibly holding the balance. The post What to Watch as New Zealand Votes Saturday appeared first on The Rio Times . (Rio Times)

wellington.title: Why Is Everyone Leaving New Zealand?
detail: Billionaires may be flocking to New Zealand, but its working-age population is leaving in droves. Many are professionals with friends and family headed to Australia. So what’s driving this exodus? (Source: Bloomberg) (Bloomberg)

wellington.title: Chris vs Chris: Who's running and what's at stake this New Zealand election
detail: New Zealanders will head to the polls on 7 November to elect a new government, with rising cost of living a key concern for voters. (BBC News)

wellington.title: New Zealand leaders make final appeals as election remains tight
detail: Polls show the election is too close to call as discontent around an ailing economy continues to swell. (The Japan Times)

wellington.title: The New Zealand Election That Could ‘Flip the Table’
detail: Support for the major parties — led by two men called Chris — is cratering, thanks to dissatisfaction with the economy. Minor parties stand to benefit from a desire among voters for change. (The New York Times)

wellington.title: New Zealand: Dead whales found as rescuers battle mass stranding
detail: Volunteers in New Zealand are working to save pilot whales stranded along the Wairarapa coast, near Cape Palliser. At least 14 have been helped back into the water, but many others have died along the remote coastline. (Euronews)

kathmandu.title: Foreign Secretary Misri sets stage for Nepal PM’s upcoming India visit
detail: The Nepali leaders expressed “gratitude for India’s swift and substantial humanitarian and technical assistance in the aftermath of the Bhotekoshi floods”, a joint press release stated (The Hindu)

kathmandu.title: Nepal’s remaining Bhutanese refugees seek legal recognition
detail: Thousands of Bhutanese refugees living in camps in Jhapa and Morang districts in eastern Nepal are still waiting for legal recognition that would allow them to work, study, and build secure lives in Nepal, more than three decades after leaving their homeland. (Inquirer)

kathmandu.title: Dashain gone, Tihar uncertain: Nepali workers stranded in Saudi Arabia as Houthi attacks disrupt flights
detail: KATHMANDU: Rajesh Rai from Khotang was preparing to return home after three years in Saudi Arabia to celebrate Dashain with family. His employer had granted him a month’s leave and he had an exit-re-entry visa. He had booked an October 11 Air Arabia flight from Riyadh to Kathmandu via Sharjah. (Dawn)

kathmandu.title: One killed after helicopters collide in Nepal
detail: Authorities have confirmed that a 47-year-old Indian national was killed and two people injured. (Al Jazeera)

An Indian national was killed and a New Zealander injured after two helicopters collided as they prepared to land in Nepal’s Mount Everest region on Tuesday, authorities said. The New Zealander has been rescued, the chief district officer of Solukhumbu district, Kaman Singh Thapa Magar, told Reuters . (Dawn)

kathmandu.title: In first high-level visit after new government’s arrival, Foreign Secretary Misri to visit Nepal on November 4-5
detail: Misri’s visit to include discussions on Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s visit to India; appointment of Nepal’s new Ambassador to India and disaster assistance following the flash floods are also expected to be on the agenda (The Hindu)

kathmandu.title: Nepal, Bhutan seek COP31 agenda on 1.5°C warming in mountain regions
detail: Nepal and Bhutan have jointly proposed the inclusion of a dedicated agenda item titled “1.5°C Warming in Mountains” at the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, calling for stronger international action to address the escalating impacts of climate change… (Inquirer)

kathmandu.title: Six Indian tourists stranded in Nepal's National Park rescued safely
detail: The Indian tourists had ventured into the area despite warnings from security personnel and the Nepali guide accompanying them, says an official (The Hindu)
